Build a feature x unit log2(Area) matrix from pep_all

Source: R/quant-stats.R
build_quant_matrix.Rd

Collapses the long pep_all table into the quantitative matrix consumed by the statistics engine. Area is summed on the linear scale across all precursors (charge states, source files) of a feature within a sample — charge states are the same molecule, so summing, not averaging, is the correct aggregation — and only then log2-transformed. Values are subsequently averaged on the log2 scale across the samples belonging to the same unit, so technical replicates collapse into their biological replicate instead of being treated as independent observations (pseudo-replication would inflate the residual degrees of freedom and make every p-value anti-conservative).

Usage

build_quant_matrix(input, feature = "Peptide", unit = "BioReplicate")

Arguments

input

A pep_all-shaped data frame (long format) with at least Area, Sample, Condition and the feature/unit columns.

feature

Column used for matrix rows: "Peptide" (default, the modified peptide sequence — the analyte in immunopeptidomics), "Sequence", "PeptideID" (precursor level) or "ProteinFirst" (parent protein).

unit

Column used for matrix columns: "BioReplicate" (default, technical replicates averaged), "Sample" (every run its own column) or "Condition".

Value

A list with mat (numeric matrix of log2 intensities, rows named by feature, columns ordered by the factor levels of unit, NAs preserved) and coldata (one row per matrix column: Unit, Condition, BioReplicate, n_Samples).

Details

Missing values are kept as NA (never 0): Area == 0 is already mapped to NA by the loaders (compute_log2area()), and the downstream steps distinguish "not detected" from "detected at low intensity".

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
qm <- build_quant_matrix(pep_all, feature = "Peptide", unit = "BioReplicate")
dim(qm$mat)
} # }
